Prevention: Select and use only borer-free seedlings and young plants for planting
Anacardiaceae (mango, cashew, etc.) family should be removed from the farm and surrounding fields, since they act as harbouring sites for borers.
If planting cocoa consider using none hosts for fruit and shade trees
Uproot and completely destroy damaged trees which serve as diapausing sites
Monitoring: Monitoring should be carried out throughout the year on aweekly basis
Inspect tree stems for entry holes and check for frass at the base of the tree or gum oozing out of the bore holes.
Also look for discolouration on stems and shoots
If in doubt, plants showing discolouration should be cut open to observe a white “larva” with a brown head and tunnels in the stem or branches
When any bore holes are observed carry out control measures
Direct Control: Plug bore holes with a stick to stop adult emerging
Heavily infested (4-5 bore holes) branches can be removed and burned.
Trees with higher infestation can be copiced.
If the infestation is low in the stem the tree should be cut.
If holes extend into the roots remove the roots too
Restrictions: Chemical pesticides are not recommended by
COCOBOD for management of this insect pest
